verses.text: This was the land given by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's oldest son. Makir was Manasseh's oldest son and the father of Gilead. Because Makir's family were great fighters, they had already received Gilead and Bashan.

So this land was for the rest of Manasseh's descendants, clan by clan: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
But Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah and Tirzah.

They went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders and said, "The LORD told Moses to give us land among our relatives." So Joshua gave them land among their father's brothers, as the LORD had commanded.
So Manasseh received ten shares of land, besides Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh's family received land along with the sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.
Manasseh's border went from Asher to Mikmethath, east of Shechem. Then it went south to the people living at En Tappuah.
The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to Ephraim.

Then the border went down to the Kanah Ravine. South of the ravine there were towns belonging to Ephraim, though they were among Manasseh's towns. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the ravine and ended at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim, and the land to the north to Manasseh. The sea was Manasseh's western border. It touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Inside the lands of Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth Shan, Ibleam, and the people of Dor, Endor, Taanach and Megiddo, each with its villages. The third one on the list was Naphoth, meaning the hills.
But the people of Manasseh could not drive out the people of these towns, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labour, but they did not drive them out completely.
Joseph's descendants said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one share of land? We are a large people, because the LORD has blessed us greatly."
Joshua answered, "If you are so many, and the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go up into the forest and clear land for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaites."
They replied, "The hill country is not big enough for us. And all the Canaanites living on the plains have iron chariots, both those in Beth Shan and its towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
But Joshua said to the descendants of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are many people, and you are very strong. You will not have only one share.
The forested hill country will be yours too. Clear it, and all of it will be yours. You can drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
